You will lay out work from blueprints, sketches, drawings and oral instructions.
You will utilize trade methods and processes to ensure conformance to requirements.
You will Install wireways, cable racks, and associated cabling to interconnect ships power, communications, lighting, fire control, instrumentation and other electrical systems.
You will troubleshoot faulty systems/circuitry to identify problem areas and initiates action to commence repairs.
Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time.Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below.This job has a screen-out element which will be used to determine minimum eligibility for this job.

Applicants who do not receive a minimum of two points on the screen-out element(s) will be found ineligible. The Screen-out Element for this position is: ABILITY TO WORK WITHOUT MORE THAN NORMAL SUPERVISION such as: Ability to read and interpret blueprints, specifications, sketches, and electrical schematics.

Proficiency in laying out work, operating various machines, and using test equipment such as multimeters, meggers, and ammeters. A working knowledge of shipboard electrical installation techniques and processes. Ability to operate a variety of power and hand tools (e.g., drill presses, hydraulic punches, grinders).

A solid mathematical background and the ability to apply electrical trade theory to perform both routine and complex work. Ability to utilize systems such as power and lighting, alarm systems, and motor controllers.

Ability to understand electrical safety practices and the ability to follow all prescribed safety rules, especially concerning energy isolation (lockout/tagout). Ability to apply electrical theory to troubleshoot faulty circuits and identify problem areas.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/federal-wage-system-qualifications/#url=List-of-Approved-Job-Elements Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

# Betriebselektriker/in Technik/Instandhaltung (m/w) #
In dieser spannenden Position sind Sie für die Gewährleistung der Anlagen-, der Betriebs- und der Arbeitssicherheit verantwortlich und beseitigen u.a. elektrische und steuerungstechnische Störungen an Produktionsanlagen.

Die elektrotechnische Instandhaltung der Produktions- und Infrastrukturanlagen obliegt Ihnen, ausserdem überwachen Sie Zutrittsberechtigung zu den Elektroanlagen. Sie unterstützen aktiv bei der kontinuierlichen Optimierung von Betriebseinrichtungen und halten die Qualitätsvorschriften und -Anforderungen sowie die Arbeitssicherheit ein (QM-System).

Das Lesen von Plänen der technischen Unterlagen und Schemata der Anlagen bereit ihnen keine Probleme. Setzen Sie mit Freude Sicherheitskonzepte um und überprüfen Sie laufend die Schutzmassnahmen und können mögliche Gefahrenstellen frühzeitig erkennen?
Als ausgebildeter Elektriker (oder ähnlich) bringen Sie Berufserfahrung als Betriebselektriker im Industrieumfeld mit und sind von Vorteil im Besitz der NIV Art. 13 Bewilligung. Sie haben gute EDV-Kenntnisse und Erfahrung mit Automationssystemen.

Sie haben eine hands-on Mentalität und packen Probleme effektiv an und können sich gut in einem grossen Anlagenbetrieb einbringen. Sie halten sich an Prozesse und helfen mit, diese stetig zu verbessern und somit zum reibungslosen Ablauf beizutragen.

Im Thema Arbeitssicherheit sind Sie versiert und sind offen für berufsbezogene interne und externe Weiterbildungen. Ihre guten IT-Kenntnisse (MS Office, SAP v.V.) sowie Deutsch als Muttersprache runden ihr Profil ab. Bereitschaft für 2-Schicht und gelegentliche Piketteinsätze sind vorhanden.
Suchen Sie eine neue Herausforderung als Betriebselektriker eines Unternehmens mit führenden, renommierten Produkten in seiner Branche? Erfüllen Sie das oben genannte Profil? Dann freuen wir uns auf Ihre vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen (Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse und Diplome) an Roman Meister, roman.meister@evergreen-hr.ch.

Help launch Sunrun's brand-new St. Louis branch! As America's #1 home solar and battery company, we are seeking an experienced Non-Certified Electrician to join our team starting now!
As a key member of our launch team, you will spend your first few months gaining hands-on leadership experience alongside our established Chicago team before permanently running installation crews out of our new St. Louis branch when doors open in early 2027.
Through our Power+ program, we invest heavily in your skills and career development, offering cross-training across solar, battery, and service operations to build long-term job security.

While supporting operations in Chicago during the pre-launch phase, Sunrun covers 100% of your travel overhead:
Rotation Schedule: 2 weeks on-site in Chicago, followed by 4 full days off at home in St. Louis.
Company Vehicle: Dedicated company vehicle provided for travel and work use.
Paid Travel Time: Full hourly compensation for time spent traveling between St. Louis and Chicago.
Lodging & Meal Allowance: 100% company-paid hotel accommodations plus daily per diem.

Electrical Installation & Interconnection: Lead or assist in the installation of electrical systems interconnecting residential solar arrays and battery storage systems to the power grid.
Service & Troubleshooting: Perform Main Panel Upgrades (MPUs), troubleshoot system issues, resolve electrical problems, and assist with necessary repairs or commissioning.
Crew Support & Leadership: Support the PV installation crew on-site and step up to lead the crew when the Foreperson is absent.
Code & Safety Compliance: Ensure work meets high workmanship standards, complies with current NEC and local codes, and strictly adheres to OSHA safety standards and Sunrun practices.
Inspections & Communication: Coordinate with local inspectors as assigned, and work closely with homeowners and branch teams to deliver a top-tier customer experience.

Education & Apprenticeship Hours: High school diploma or equivalent. Must possess 75% of the hours required to sit for state-specific electrical certification exams (Certified Electrical Trainee preferred or required depending on state regulations).
Electrical Experience: Hands-on electrical installation and repair experience, including work with wiring up to 600 VDC / 480 VAC. Working knowledge of replacing residential electrical services and distribution panels preferred.
Technical & Code Proficiency: Working knowledge of NEC codes, ability to interpret single-line drawings/PV system schematics from roof to meter, and solid understanding of solar interconnection principles and basic construction.
Driver Requirements: Must be at least 21 years old with a valid driver's license and a clean driving record (ability to pass a driving background check).
Soft Skills & Ownership: Strong troubleshooting and logical decision-making skills, customer focus, and a results-driven attitude with the ability to lead when necessary.
Physical Demands
Lifting & Transport: Ability to regularly transport materials and equipment up to 50 lbs (and up to 100 lbs with assistance).
Heights & Confined Spaces: Comfortable working on rooftops at various pitch angles, walking on rafters/shingles without causing damage, and maneuvering in attics, basements, or crawl spaces.
PPE & Safety Gear: Ability to work safely while wearing heavy protective equipment, including arc flash suits, gloves, face shields, and fall protection harnesses.
Environmental Exposure: Ability to work outdoors in varied weather conditions (extreme heat/cold, humidity, wet environments), low-light or full-sun settings, and around standard chemical materials.
Vision & Physical Function: Fine motor skills (manipulation, grasping, pinching), normal color vision (ability to distinguish wiring colors such as red, black, yellow, white, green), and clear hearing for safety commands.

## **Ta mission :** ##
En tant que technicien électricien, tu rejoins une activité spécialisée dans l-installation, le montage, la mise en service et la maintenance de groupes électrogènes de secours.
Issu du domaine de l-électricité du bâtiment, tu souhaites aujourd-hui faire évoluer ton parcours vers un environnement plus industriel et technique. Une formation spécifique te permettra de développer progressivement tes compétences et de te spécialiser dans ce domaine.
Ton activité se répartit entre environ 60 % de travail en atelier et 40 % d-interventions sur chantier.

* Participer au montage et au câblage électrique des groupes électrogènes de secours
* Préparer les équipements, composants et matériels nécessaires aux interventions
* Réaliser les raccordements électriques et les adaptations techniques nécessaires
* Participer à l-installation des groupes électrogènes directement sur les sites clients
* Effectuer les contrôles, essais et mises en service des installations
* Lire et interpréter les plans, schémas électriques et documents techniques
* Rechercher et identifier les éventuels défauts électriques
* Participer aux opérations de maintenance préventive et corrective
* Effectuer les travaux d-entretien, de dépannage et de remise en service
* Réaliser les modifications et adaptations nécessaires sur les installations existantes
* Collaborer avec les techniciens et les différents intervenants sur chantier
* Assurer le service de piquet selon le tournus et le planning établi
* Intervenir en cas de dépannage urgent durant les périodes de piquet
* Respecter les procédures techniques ainsi que les règles de sécurité
* Maintenir un environnement de travail propre, organisé et sécurisé

Tu disposes d-au moins 5 à 6 années d-expérience dans l-électricité du bâtiment et souhaites aujourd-hui donner une nouvelle orientation à ton parcours professionnel en te spécialisant dans un domaine technique lié à l-industrie.
Une expérience préalable dans les groupes électrogènes n-est pas indispensable. Ce qui compte avant tout, c-est ta solide expérience pratique en électricité, ta motivation à apprendre et ton envie de développer de nouvelles compétences.

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most blue-collar positions, you must meet any screen-out element listed, and show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

JOB ELEMENTS: Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of safety regulations and procedures. 2.

Knowledge of electrical theory, principles, standard trade methods and practices, and circuitry; aircraft electrical systems and their interrelationships; electronics principles (e.g., knowledge of construction practices of electronic equipment to recognize types and sizes of resistors, capacitors, wiring, and transistors); knowledge to follow signal paths through printed circuit and wired circuitry to recognize actual circuit configurations shown in schematics and diagrams; the electromagnetic basis of alternating current and inductive and capacitance reactance, series and parallel tuned circuits, impedance matching, and operation of transistors to troubleshoot, modify, repair, overhaul, and maintain complex electrical systems such as antiskid, automatic flight control, and fuel indicating systems; and knowledge of the interface of electrical systems with hydraulic, electronic armament, instrument, and mechanical systems and assemblies. 3.

Operates and/or uses and maintains all types of equipment and tools common to the utility trade including, but not limited to, multiple-drive vehicles, bull dozers, truck-mounted augers, compressors, winch trucks, truck/trailer combinations, bucket and/or crane or boom trucks, truck-operated winch, and digging tools.

Works on energized lines (up to 161-kV) requiring the use of safety devices such as, but not limited to, hot line tools, rubber gloves, and mats.

Performs other duties as required in the daily work, which may include such items as patrolling lines; digging pole and anchor holes; back filling; banking poles; cutting brush, weeds, and trees; and repairing roads, bridges, fences, and gates along rights-of-way.

Investigates, as requested, transmission line equipment failures/interruptions, diagnosing problems and determining possible remedies (troubleshooting).

Contacts are with agency personnel, officials and employees of other Federal agencies, and external customers including landowners, contractors, linemen, and representative s of private utilities and like organizations.

The purpose of the contacts is to plan, coordinate maintenance and construction work efforts, exchange information, or to resolve operating problems. Contacts are usually working toward mutual goals and generally have cooperative attitudes.
Qualifications: You must have journeyman-level ability in the duties of a High Voltage Electrician (Lineman). You must meet all the qualification and eligibility requirements for the position by the closing date of the announcement.

In order to qualify for this position, your resume must provide sufficient experience and/or education, knowledge, skills, and abilities, to perform the duties of the specific position for which you are being considered. Your resume is the key means we have for evaluating your skills, knowledge, and abilities, as they relate to this position.

Therefore, we encourage you to submit a thorough resume that directly relates to this position. Applicants must meet the requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Job Qualification System for Trades and Labor Occupations (X-118C).

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on the quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below. Your resume should demonstrate that you possess these elements and screen out.

Do not provide a separate narrative written statement. Rather, you must describe in your resume how your past work experience demonstrates that you possess the elements and screen out identified below. The screen-out element for this position is below.

Failure to meet this Screen out Element will result in an ineligible rating: Ability to do the work of a journeyman lineman constructing and maintaining transmission or distribution power lines (69KV or higher) and related equipment independently without greater than normal supervision.

If your knowledge and ability in the SCREEN OUT factor above is not sufficient, you will receive no further consideration. In preparing your application, describe in detail the experience and training which you have had that specifically prepared you for this job and to perform the duties described for this job.

Experience should be clearly described and documented in your resume. The qualifications reviewer will not assume performance of such duties by Job Titles alone. "Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience.

Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Physical Effort: The work requires physical exertion such as heavy lifting and carrying (up to 100 pounds) over rough terrain, i.e., one end of an assembled 34-foot cross arm or a string of suspension insulators.

Frequent pulling and or pushing, often from awkward positions, i.e., dinging and un-dinging suspension insulators while in hooks, requiring the use of both legs; climbing wooden poles using climbers and steel towers with steps or step bolts while wearing gear weighing approximately 35 pounds, requiring the use of both legs; frequent use of hands and fingers requiring the use of both hands and all fingers; moderate walking over rough terrain, stooping and kneeling, and standing for long periods.

Work Condition: The work environment involves high risks, with exposure to potentially dangerous situations or unusual environmental stress, such as working with high-voltage electrical equipment (.001 volts to 161,000 volts as general criteria), in remote, outdoor field locations with rough terrain; and exposure to various weather conditions, wind, dust, brush, insects, and occasionally poisonous snakes; and emergency situations at all hours of the day and any day.

Position may require accredited nationally recognized certification for fixed and swing boom cranes, aerial man-lifts, and/or material handling equipment. If so, training will be provided at government expense. The general public will be encountered, who may object to aspects of the projects.

Travel to and lodging at remote locations is frequently required. Travel is by motor vehicle, aircraft, or other means of transportation. Limit your resume to no more than two (2) pages. If more than two pages are submitted, only the first two pages will be reviewed to determine your eligibility and qualifications.
